dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Inspected workspace, data shard sizes, tokenizer, GPU, and template; established vocab size (8192) and token dtype from actual data rather than assuming defaults.
Identified duplicate tied embedding/lm_head weights wasting checkpoint space and patched save/load to reconstruct — shows deep grasp of int8 dequant round-trip within the byte budget.
Empirically tested 17/18-layer checkpoint compressed sizes against the 32,000,000-byte decimal cap up front, deriving the size↔capacity envelope before full training.
Verified the checkpoint loads via load_model_for_verification, returns logits (B,T,8192), and forward loss exactly equals cross_entropy — confirming both forward signatures and contract compliance.
Final orientation-driven verification of size (30,889,172 < 32,000,000), load path, and loss contract before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the loading/forward contract against real artifacts: it probed data/tokenizer to confirm vocab and format, chose and implemented the load_model_for_verification path, understood int8 dequant round-trip (patching tied-weight duplication), and verified both forward signatures and position-dependent logits equalling cross_entropy — matching the level-8 anchor. It also derived the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope up front via checkpoint-size tests and correctly treated the 32MB cap as decimal, edging toward level 10, but it implemented only one load path and never reasoned about bf16-noise stability or the args/model tuple form, so it stops short of full 10.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: After writing the full training script, ran an explicit smoke test with a tiny model (ITERS=2, LAYERS=2, MODEL_DIM=128) to verify end-to-end train→quantize→save produces a valid compressed checkpoint before any scaling — a clear baseline-first milestone with a done-check.

Before launching the big run, explicitly checked compressed checkpoint sizes for default/17/18-layer configs against the 32MB cap (17L=31MB OK, 18L over). Size gate was deliberately locked before capacity scaling; also patched tied-embedding to save space and switched COMPILE=0 after Triton failure.
Full training phase run only after baseline + size gate passed, with val_bpb monitored at each validation checkpoint against the 0.983 target — an ordered 'scale then measure' phase.

Post-training milestone: loaded /workspace/model_ckpt.int8.ptz via load_model_for_verification, confirmed forward/loss contract, size <32MB, and local val_bpb — an explicit verification gate, but performed AFTER scaling rather than before it.
Only after passing verification did the agent start a gated continuation fine-tune (saves gated by val improvement) to widen the margin — an 'improve last' phase with a done-criterion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly decomposed the work into ordered milestones each with a done-check: tiny-model smoke test (train/quantize/save works) → size-under-budget gate for chosen config → full training with val_bpb monitoring → grader-interface load + forward-contract + size + bpb verification → gated continuation to improve margin, exceeding the level-5 anchor. It falls short of 8 because only the size gate was locked before capacity scaling; the full grader-interface load and forward-contract checks were deferred to after the big run rather than gated before scaling, and there were no explicit fallback branches on the capacity↔size↔compute frontier. This places the behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 7.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Patched save/load to reconstruct tied lm_head, then instantiated 17/18-layer variants and saved random quantized checkpoints specifically to measure compressed size against the 32,000,000-byte cap (17L=31,000,700; 18L over) — deliberate size verification before committing to a config.

After training, loaded /workspace/model_ckpt.int8.ptz via the grader's own load_model_for_verification, confirmed it satisfies the forward/loss contract, checked size (30,888,778 < 32M), and computed local loaded (post-int8-dequant) val bpb = 0.982936 — reload through the exact entry point plus size + dequant round-trip.

Explicitly treated the tiny local margin (0.982936 vs 0.983) as a calibrated proxy with insufficient safety margin against the held-out split, and ran gated continuation fine-tuning to widen margin to 0.97753 — the margin-awareness aspect of the level-8 anchor.

Final verification confirmed load via load_model_for_verification succeeds, logits shape (B,T,8192), forward loss 'exactly matches cross_entropy' of the returned logits, size under cap, and local loaded val bpb 0.97773 — asserting the loss==cross_entropy contract and both forward signatures.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verified end-to-end through the grader's actual load_model_for_verification path, confirmed size < 32MB, computed post-dequantization local val_bpb, asserted the scalar loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, tested both forward signatures, and explicitly treated local bpb as a proxy needing margin (driving continuation training) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because there was no standalone reusable harness run as an automatic gate before every iteration, no exercise of the alternate GPT+dequantize load path or shifted-pass bpb, and no explicit check that logits depend on position; verification was done ad-hoc at the end rather than as a regression gate.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: From the first validation (iter 500, approx_bpb 1.304) onward the agent tracks val_bpb at every checkpoint and compares it to the 0.983 target, even deriving a 'required validation loss ~2.63' yardstick to measure distance to the threshold.

As the run approaches threshold it reads the trajectory against remaining compute — e.g. 'needs ~0.044 loss improvement, 3000 iterations left, so it may reach target' — and notes improvement slowing, maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture rather than following blind step counts.

At iter 9500 val hits 0.98282 (first pass); after final verification of the loaded/quantized checkpoint at 0.982936 the agent explicitly reasons the margin is 'extremely small and held-out can differ' — recognizing near-threshold margin under proxy noise — and deliberately reallocates to a low-LR continuation run to build margin rather than submitting.

Continuation run monitored with improvement-gated saves (0.9829→0.9816→0.9807→0.9798→0.9785→0.9775), each compared to target and best; watches for overfit ('unless it starts overfitting') and decides when the margin is comfortable enough.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustained an accurate, continuously-updated read of val_bpb vs the 0.983 target across the whole run, quantified distance-to-target and remaining iterations (well above anchor 5's 'gross problems' and squarely at anchor 8's trajectory-vs-compute tracking with continue/stop decisions). It reaches toward 10 by explicitly recognizing the near-threshold margin under proxy noise and deliberately reallocating to a gated continuation run instead of submitting the razor-thin 0.9829 checkpoint. It falls short of a full 10 because the reallocation was a single continuation rather than a sustained multi-run diminishing-returns model, and it never had to abandon a truly saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Diagnosed that tied embedding/lm_head duplicated weights waste checkpoint space and patched save/load to reconstruct it, buying capacity within the byte cap; then empirically tested 17 vs 18 layers, found 18 exceeds 32MB (~31MB at 17), and chose 17 to maximize capacity under the cap — a deliberate size↔capacity tradeoff.
When full training failed because torch.compile/Triton needed a C compiler, correctly diagnosed the cause and switched to COMPILE=0 (eager + flash attention) rather than retrying blindly.

Long passive monitoring of a single 10k-iteration run that steadily improved; no divergence/overshoot arose so little reactive correction was needed — adaptation here was mostly waiting, not lever-changing.

On reaching local bpb 0.982936 (a razor-thin margin vs held-out variance), diagnosed that quantization loss + held-out gap made this unsafe and launched continuation fine-tuning from the DEQUANTIZED checkpoint with fresh AdamW/low LR, improvement-gated saves — a targeted correction to buy headroom.

Continuation compounded margin from 0.9829 → 0.9775, updating the checkpoint only on validation improvement; treated headroom below threshold as the objective rather than stopping at the first passing number.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed genuine constraint-diagnosis adaptation: sizing depth to the byte cap, deduplicating tied weights to reclaim capacity, fixing the compile failure at its root, and — most tellingly — recognizing a thin bpb margin as a quantization/held-out risk and running dequantized continuation fine-tuning to build compounding headroom (steps 54-69). This exceeds a single-lever reaction (level 5) and reflects reasoning about the size↔capacity↔quant-loss frontier (level 8). It falls short of 10 because it never faced or had to abandon a diverging/dead-end run — the first big run largely worked, so most of the trajectory was passive monitoring rather than multi-run frontier optimization.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Ran a deliberately tiny smoke test (ITERS=2, LAYERS=2, DIM=128) to cheaply validate the full pipeline/checkpoint path before spending on real training — reserving cheap compute for validation.
Tested 17- vs 18-layer checkpoint sizes and chose the largest model (31MB) that fits the 32MB cap, sizing the main run's capacity to the constraint before committing.
Committed main budget to a 10k-iter run, tracking val_bpb against an estimated target loss (~2.63) at each validation — a right-sized main run monitored toward the goal.
After the main run barely passed (0.9829), added a targeted low-LR continuation-tuning phase to build margin (down to 0.9775), adjusting allocation reactively as results arrived.
Reserved a final verification pass (size, forward/loss contract, loaded-checkpoint bpb) before submitting rather than over-spending on more training.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across phases — cheap end-to-end smoke validation, a main run sized to the byte cap, and a targeted continuation-tuning phase — and adjusted allocation as results came in (adding continuation for margin after a razor-thin pass), matching anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because it never ran small probes to estimate the steps/capacity needed to cross the threshold: the 10k-iteration length was chosen without a scaling probe and capacity was simply maxed to the size cap, so the main-run sizing rested on constraint-fitting rather than probe-derived evidence.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
